chunks: My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd Al-Yaqťini, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il Al-Basri, from someone who narrated to him, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: The sacred boundary (hurmat) of the grave of Al-Husayn is one parasang by one parasang from each of its four sides.

key_terms.حُرْمَةُ: Sacred boundary or sanctity; a legal status conferring respect and specific rulings.
key_terms.فَرْسَخٌ: Parasang, a traditional unit of distance (approx. 5-6 km).

ai.seo_question: What is the defined sacred boundary of Imam Al-Husayn's grave?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the *hurmat* (sanctity) of Imam Al-Husayn’s grave as a square area extending one parasang (approx. 5-6 km) in each cardinal direction, a measurement rooted in early Islamic geographical units. This specific boundary grants the surrounding land a legal status of reverence, influencing rituals of respect and prohibiting actions that might desecrate the site, thereby emphasizing the physical space as an extension of the Imam’s spiritual presence.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father and all of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā ibn ‘Ubayd Al-Yaqťīni, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl Al-Basri, from someone who narrated to him, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.))
said: The sacred boundaries of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) are one parasang by one parasang from each of its four sides.
